options.label: Domain-first framing

previewBlocks.code:
Q1: What exists right now?
  -> Search + ingestion + persisted observations

Q2: Can I trust where this came from?

Q3: Can I operate it live?

Q4: Can an agent use it programmatically?

slides.title: 2) Source coherency: one truth, no alias drift
slides.context: Recent refactor intent: stop runtime alias ambiguity.

previewBlocks.content:
flowchart TD
  I[Incoming source string] --> R[sourceRegistry.resolveCanonicalSource]
  R --> N[sourceResolver.normalizeToCanonicalSource]
  N --> E[toEcsIntelSource]
  E --> P[Persistence + Provenance]
  N --> U[UI / Search / Filters use canonical IDs]

previewBlocks.code:
Without canonicalization:
- Source counts split across aliases
- Filter toggles mismatch actual backend sources
- Provenance confidence fragmented
- Tool output inconsistent with UI labels

With canonicalization:
- One source ID per concept
- Stable aggregation and filtering
- Deterministic provenance and diagnostics

slides.title: 3) What happens when you run a search
slides.context: User click, service fan-out, normalized results, UI render.

previewBlocks.content:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as Search UI
  participant M as SearchMachine
  participant RPC as SearchRpcServer
  participant H as SearchEntityHandlers
  participant Repo as Repositories/APIs
  participant Map as Result Mapper

  UI->>M: execute(bounds, sources)
  M->>RPC: searchInBounds/searchNearby
  RPC->>H: dispatch by source
  H->>Repo: query source backends
  Repo-->>H: raw records
  H->>Map: SearchResult* constructors
  Map-->>RPC: canonical SearchResultItem[]
  RPC-->>M: grouped results + source counts/errors
  M-->>UI: render list/map + statuses

previewBlocks.code:
SearchMachine owns interaction state:
- selected sources
- in-flight status per source
- progress + errors

Search services own data retrieval:
- source-specific fetch/query
- transformation to SearchResultItem
- normalized source accounting

slides.title: 4) From result to living entity (stx + traits)
slides.context: How a result becomes stateful, reactive runtime data.

previewBlocks.content:
flowchart LR
  SR[SearchResultItem] --> GE[GeointEntity.fromSearchResult]
  GE --> TR[Trait mapping]
  TR --> SX[entity-stx instance
(one per entity)]
  SX --> FM[Trait Fermions
(one per trait type)]
  SX --> UI[Map markers / cards / detail panels]
  SX --> OPS[Entity ops: select, focus, update, remove]

previewBlocks.code:
Think of stx as the per-entity brain:
- identity + lifecycle status
- current derived view state
- links to trait-level behavior

Think of Fermions as specialist reflexes:
- one for flight-like behavior
- one for weather-like behavior
- one for imagery/feature behavior

slides.title: 6) Coherency check: what we validate to trust the stack
slides.context: If these pass, architecture is aligned end-to-end.

previewBlocks.code:
A. Source ID coherence
  - no runtime adsb_lol literals
  - no runtime source:'weather' in SearchResult paths
  - canonical IDs resolve consistently

B. Search pipeline coherence
  - SearchMachine sources == schema literals
  - RPC sourceCounts/sourceErrors keyed by canonical IDs

C. Entity coherence
  - GeointEntity factory accepts updated source IDs
  - materializers map source -> ECS intel source deterministically

D. Tooling coherence
  - geoint_* tools and sdk.geoint.* return consistent source IDs

E. Regression coherence
  - targeted vitest suites green

Most likely drift points:
1) testbeds and fixture payloads
2) UI source icon/label maps
3) registry alias tables
4) backend source fan-out defaults
5) docs that still describe legacy IDs as runtime values
